title: UNI: a general-purpose foundation model for computational pathology
summary: Archived from discovery counts: this entry documents retrospective method benchmarks rather than a qualifying scientific discovery. UNI was pretrained on more than 100 million image patches from over 100,000 H&E whole-slide images across 20 major tissue types. Across 34 pathology tasks, including cancer classification and transplant-rejection assessment, it outperformed established pathology AI models. Evaluation is retrospective, and the weights are gated under a non-commercial academic licence.
ai_technology: UNI (self-supervised vision transformer foundation model for pathology)
organization: Mass General Brigham; Harvard Medical School

title: NatureLM-audio: an audio-language model for bioacoustics
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the November 2024 preprint evaluates a bioacoustics model on benchmark tasks rather than reporting a new biological finding or a field-study result. NatureLM-audio achieved 19.6% accuracy for scientific-name classification of unseen species and 38.3% accuracy for counting zebra finch individuals in recordings. These are evaluations on BEANS-Zero, not discovery of new species or interpretation of animal communication; the historical entry is retained as method-development context.

title: Prov-GigaPath: a whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology
summary: Archived from discovery counts: this paper introduces a foundation model and evaluates retrospective prediction benchmarks rather than reporting a separate biological finding or clinical field-study result. Prov-GigaPath was pretrained on 1.3 billion image tiles from 171,189 whole-slide images of more than 30,000 patients across 31 tissue types. It led on 25 of 26 evaluated tasks using both Providence and TCGA data, so evaluation was not confined to one health network. The historical entry is retained as method-development context, consistently with the archived UNI entry.
ai_technology: Prov-GigaPath (GigaPath vision transformer with LongNet dilated attention)
organization: Microsoft Research; Providence; University of Washington

title: Boltz-1: an open model for biomolecular structures
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the December 2024 announcement and original Boltz-1 report introduce an open biomolecular structure-prediction model and compare it with AlphaFold3 and Chai-1 on CASP15 and held-out Protein Data Bank structures. These are method benchmarks; the reviewed release does not identify a separate biological finding or qualifying application result. Model weights, training and inference code were released openly. The historical entry is retained as method-development context, consistently with the archived UNI entry.

title: Cellpose 2.0: human-in-the-loop training for cell segmentation
summary: Archived from discovery counts: Cellpose 2.0 develops and evaluates cell-segmentation and annotation tools on existing Cellpose, TissueNet and LiveCell images. Fine-tuning used 500-1,000 annotated regions, or roughly 100-200 with human-in-the-loop annotation. The paper investigates segmentation accuracy, annotation styles and annotation effort; it does not report a distinct biological finding from those images. This is method-development evidence, retained as historical context consistently with the archived UNI entry.
ai_technology: Cellpose 2.0 (deep learning cell segmentation, human-in-the-loop fine-tuning)

title: Review of AI methods for designing physics experiments
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the September 2026 Nature article is a Review of AI-assisted experimental design, not a report of a new experiment or a distinct original discovery established by this entry. It organizes prior work around search spaces, simulators, scientific objectives and exploration methods. The reviewed examples retain their original research dates; this historical entry preserves the review as context rather than counting those examples again as a September 2026 result.
ai_technology: AI-driven optimisation of experimental setups (Krenn group method, simulation-based search)
organization: University of Tübingen; TU Wien; University of Vienna

title: Co-Scientist and ALS: hypotheses about RNA-based mechanisms
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the represented announcement describes hypothesis generation and a research collaboration, without a reported experimental result. Two groups, at MIT (Ritu Raman) and Boston Children's Hospital (Ryan Flynn), used Co-Scientist to assess a conflicting literature, turn ideas into testable hypotheses, and rank them by feasibility, focusing on RNA-based mechanisms and drugs. The post reports no quantitative results or experimental validation; the research is ongoing.
organization: Google DeepMind; MIT, and Boston Children's Hospital

evidence.tested: No validation or experimental results are reported; Co-Scientist's ideas were ranked by feasibility and risk-reward and the research is described as ongoing.
evidence.unknown: The post states that Co-Scientist cannot do science alone and that the best leads needed molecular expertise the team lacked; no formal limitations are listed.
evidence.ai_role: Co-Scientist assessed the contradictory ALS literature, generated testable hypotheses and ranked research directions focused on RNA-based mechanisms.

title: Co-Scientist and molecular switches in severe infectious diseases
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the represented announcement describes hypotheses and cell lines still being prepared to test them, not a completed biological result. Clare Bryant (Cambridge) used Co-Scientist, which ranked hypotheses and pointed to a protein she had not considered down to individual amino acids, to study molecular switches behind diseases such as sepsis. The lab expects to build cell lines with those mutations in about six months instead of two or three years; the hypotheses are not yet validated.
organization: Google DeepMind; and University of Cambridge

evidence.tested: The hypotheses are not validated; the lab is building cell lines with the proposed amino acid mutations to test them, and the page reports no results.
evidence.unknown: The page states only that the six-month estimate holds if the targets are right; the publication status is not stated.
evidence.ai_role: Co-Scientist generated and ranked hypotheses from the grant proposal and narrowed candidate proteins to specific amino acids.

title: Perch: an open bioacoustics model to protect endangered species
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the represented event updates a bioacoustics model; the application outcomes described concern its predecessor rather than a new result from this release. The updated Perch model, released openly, predicts bird species better than its predecessor and has nearly twice as much training data (birds, mammals, amphibians, and human noise). The post gives no numbers for the new model; results on Hawaiian honeycreeper detection are from the earlier model.

evidence.tested: Perch 2.0 was evaluated on the BirdSet and BEANS benchmarks and on marine transfer-learning tasks against specialized marine models.
evidence.unknown: The abstract lists no explicit limitations, and its explanations for why the pre-training works are hypotheses.
evidence.ai_role: An open bioacoustics model was trained on bird, mammal, amphibian and human-noise audio to classify species.

title: OMol25 and UMA: quantum-chemistry data and a universal model for atoms
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the represented event releases a molecular dataset and an interatomic model, without identifying a specific new chemical finding or application outcome. Meta released Open Molecules 2025, which it calls the largest and most varied set of high-accuracy quantum calculations for biomolecules, metal complexes, and electrolytes (about six billion compute hours), and UMA, an interatomic potential trained on over 30 billion atoms. The post gives no numerical accuracy values.

evidence.unknown: The post gives no numerical accuracy values or evaluation method, and no limitations are stated.
evidence.ai_role: A machine learning interatomic potential (UMA) was trained on the OMol25 calculations and data from Meta's datasets.

title: DolphinGemma: a model for finding patterns in dolphin sounds
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the represented event introduces a model and planned field use, without establishing a new finding about dolphin communication. A model with about 400 million parameters, trained on decades of recordings of Atlantic spotted dolphins from the Wild Dolphin Project, predicts subsequent sounds to identify recurring patterns; it runs on Pixel phones used in the field. The patterns have not been confirmed to carry meaning.
organization: Google; Georgia Tech, and Wild Dolphin Project

evidence.unknown: The source describes only early field testing with no quantitative metrics, the model is trained on one dolphin population, and the patterns are not confirmed to carry meaning.
evidence.ai_role: A roughly 400M-parameter audio model predicted likely next dolphin sounds to find recurring patterns.

title: Physics-based differentiable imaging detects 51 Eridani b in a JWST band where standard processing did not
summary: Archived from discovery counts: the lead researchers explicitly state that FLIP did not use AI. Its automatic-differentiation tools optimize a physics-based instrument model. A physics-based coronagraph model optimized with automatic differentiation and gradient descent recovered 51 Eridani b in JWST/NIRCam F430M images at 4.3 μm, where the published standard-processing result was a non-detection. The paper also reports two- to fifteen-fold sensitivity gains across its test observations.
ai_technology: FLIP (Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets), a differentiable instrument model optimized with automatic differentiation
organization: Northwestern University; California Institute of Technology; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Space Telescope Science Institute

evidence.tested: A physics-based coronagraph model optimized with automatic differentiation and gradient descent recovered 51 Eridani b in JWST/NIRCam F430M images at 4.3 μm, where the published standard-processing result was a non-detection.
evidence.unknown: The planet 51 Eridani b was already discovered by ground-based imaging in 2015; the new finding is its first JWST image in the 4.3 μm carbon-dioxide band, not discovery of a previously unknown planet. Performance estimates are based on a limited set of three target systems and should not be generalized to all JWST data.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers state that this work did not use AI, although it used computational tools also used to train AI models. FLIP optimized a physics-based telescope model using automatic differentiation.

title: AJIN machine learning predicts atomic layer deposition outcomes from experimental precursor-substrate data
summary: Archived as a method-development and transfer benchmark. AJIN predicts adsorption and deposition outcomes for atomic layer deposition. The November 5, 2026 preprint compares predictions with literature data and the authors’ laboratory cases, but the reviewed abstract and results section 3.7 do not identify a separate new material, deposition chemistry or scientific finding enabled by the model. Laboratory comparison alone does not turn this general prediction method into a qualifying discovery. The historical ID and source are retained outside discovery counts.
ai_technology: AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network) with graph-neural-network embeddings (CHGNet-MLP best model)
organization: Incheon National University; Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Literature-data classification and comparison with laboratory transfer cases; no separate new chemistry result identified in reviewed sections.
evidence.unknown: Retained outside discovery counts as a historical method demonstration. This is an admission decision, not a claim that experiments were absent. Physical prediction-before-assay timing was not established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning framework predicting whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields ALD, with SHAP and ablation analyses of the drivers.

title: MarsNet learns the Martian atmosphere from observations alone
summary: Archived as a model-development and atmospheric-reanalysis benchmark. The November 9, 2026 MarsNet preprint evaluates temperature and pressure estimates against held-out Martian observations. The reviewed abstract and discussion describe improved near-surface estimation and possible future uses as a discovery tool, rather than a separate atmospheric finding. The authors note poorer performance aloft and that much temperature skill precedes neural training. The historical ID and source are retained outside discovery counts.
ai_technology: MarsNet, a learned forecast-and-update model with a fixed physical structure and bounded Kalman update

evidence.tested: Retrospective comparison with held-out Mars temperatures and pressures; no separate atmospheric discovery identified.
evidence.unknown: Retained outside discovery counts; the exclusion does not dispute model skill. Held-out MY32 also informed run selection; no prospective field test established.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network learns the forecast tendencies and the observation update jointly, inside a fixed physical structure, and the influence of each observation can be traced.

title: Claude designs three working electronics prototypes built and tested by an external manufacturer
summary: Archived as an engineering-capability demonstration without a separate scientific result. Anthropic’s November 9, 2026 announcement describes Claude Fable 5.2 designing three electronics prototypes assembled by collaborator Diode Computers. This source check covered the original announcement. The microphone-port example concerns the voice-assistant hub, not the speakerphone. Functional prototypes and design benchmarks do not by themselves establish a qualifying scientific discovery; commercial certification and durability were not established. The historical ID and source are retained outside discovery counts.
ai_technology: Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) as electronics design agent

evidence.tested: Physical assembly and operation of three collaborator-built electronics prototypes; no separate scientific finding identified.
evidence.unknown: Retained outside discovery counts. Diode is a collaborator, not independent replication. No certification or long-term outcome established.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Fable 5.2 generated electronic and mechanical designs, firmware and assembly instructions; Diode built the prototypes.

title: AutoDNA: an AI-native autonomous laboratory for biomolecular engineering
summary: AutoDNA is an AI-native biomolecular laboratory platform from Shanghai Jiao Tong University. The 2026-11-04 journal abstract reports orchestration of more than 20 instrument types over more than 11,000 steps, expert-level DNA-synthesis yields, 3.2-fold faster concurrent protocol execution, exact recovery of DNA-stored digital content and detection/validation of a known KRAS G13D mutation. Archived as platform and workflow validation: the reviewed material identifies no separate new biological finding or clinical study result qualifying as a catalog discovery.
ai_technology: AutoDNA AI-native autonomous laboratory (co-designed models, experiments and instruments)

evidence.tested: Four platform demonstrations: enzymatic DNA synthesis, concurrent execution, DNA data storage and detection/validation of a known KRAS G13D mutation.
evidence.unknown: Publisher main body is paywalled; scope was the abstract, affiliations, date, figure titles, captions and accessible back matter. No claim of full-paper review or absence of every possible application is made.
evidence.ai_role: AI models co-designed with experiments and instruments orchestrate the end-to-end workflow autonomously.

title: LPT: bounded agentic LLM loops for de novo protein binder design
summary: The LPT preprint describes fixed, bounded LLM-agent stages with access to a literature database of about 14,000 papers. A database-backed model answered 41 of 48 benchmark questions, versus none without access. Three binder-design demonstrations targeted CALCRL/RAMP1, PD-1/PD-L1 and PVR–TIGIT, with evaluation by other folding models. Archived as a computational workflow/method benchmark: the reviewed abstract establishes no binding measurement or separately validated scientific result.
ai_technology: LPT framework: fixed orchestration of bounded LLM agentic loops with literature database and design tools

evidence.tested: Question-answering benchmark and three computational binder-design campaigns checked using multiple structure-prediction models.
evidence.unknown: Abstract and original-server metadata reviewed. No claim that the inaccessible full paper contains no experiments is made; the reviewed abstract reports only in-silico performance.
evidence.ai_role: LLM stages identified the design intent, selected targets, structures and hotspot residues, and designed candidate binders.
